units.signature: fn fz_count[&h](heap: &!h Heap, n: int) -> [heap] int
units.description: A helper the brief does not name: it may take a heap.
tests: pub fn test_fz_count_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert(fz_count(heap, 3) == 3); return 0; }

units.signature: fn edit_distance[&h, &a, &b](heap: &!h Heap, a: &a [byte], b: &b [byte]) -> [heap] int
tests: pub fn test_dist_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert(edit_distance(heap, "kitten", "sitting") == 3); return 0; }

units.description: Its result owns memory: the heap is the caller's.
tests: pub fn test_pick_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match closest(heap, "abc") { option.Option::Some(b) => { buffer.drop(heap, b); test.assert(false); } option.Option::None => { test.assert(true); } } return 0; }
pub fn test_rom_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match from_roman(heap, "XIV") { result.Result::Ok(v) => { test.assert(v == 14); } result.Result::Err(e) => { test.assert(false); } } return 0; }

units.signature: fn fz_free_count[&h](heap: &!h Heap, parts: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] int
units.description: Takes the list by value and frees it: the heap is needed for that, so `brief-heap` leaves it alone.
tests: pub fn test_free_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert(fz_free_count(heap, list.empty()) == 0); return 0; }
